To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

high quantitative demands, information- and communication technology ( ICT) demands, under qualification, conflicts and poor social support were positively associated with current and future cognitive complaints, while high skill discretion, decision authority, good resources at the workplace and high qualification were negatively associated with current and/or future cognitive complaints.
psychosocial factors are associated with both current and future cognitive complaints among the general population.

quantitative demands, ICT demands, underqualification, conflicts, skill discretion and resources are associated with cognitive complaints among employees, and that these associations are independent of depressive- and sleeping complaints.

the associations between psychsoical work factors and cognitive problems.
cognitive complaints in the work force and the role of psychosocial working factors in these complaints.

the associations between psychometrically measured psychosocial working factors and cognitive complaints, in nationally representative samples from the Swedish work force, using a cross-sectional design and a prospective design.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

high quantitative demands, ICT demands, underqualification, conflicts, low social support, low skill discretion, low decision authority and low resources were associated with cognitive complaints among employees in Sweden.
psychosocial work conditions play an important role in cognitive complaints, and should be taken into consideration when investigating cognitive complaints.

quantitative demands, ICT demands, underqualification, conflicts, skill discretion and resources are associated with cognitive complaints among employees, while social support and decision authority seem to protect against cognitive complaints.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
psychosocial work conditions, including both positive and negative factors, are associated with cognitive complaints among Swedish employees.

psychosocial work characteristics may have an impact on the development of cognitive complaints, but the impact is small and may be mediated by depressive symptoms, sleeping problems, and baseline cognitive complaints.
cognitive complaints are related to a number of psychosocial working factors.
The main takeaway from our work is that

psychosocial factors, particularly quantitative demands and ICT demands, are associated with cognitive complaints and that these associations are not fully explained by general confounders or by depressive and sleeping problems.
psychosocial work conditions are related to cognitive complaints, and that these associations are not explained by depressive- or sleeping problems.
psychosocial work environment factors, particularly quantitative demands and conflicts, are related to cognitive complaints among employees, and that these relationships persist over time.
